title: situsAddress is the leaf nobody graded
mergeSha: not applicable: lane instructed not to merge
missionPremise: hauska-factory verify-walk.mjs requires baseFacts.situsAddress as a four-state (BP-CONTENT-01) and legacy-design-tools' BAKE_OWNED_REQUIRED_LEAF_PATHS did not include it, so the leaf was graded by a ~180-parcel sample downstream and owned by no control at the write. Three of the six CTX counties passed their 2026-09-10 staging walk while serving a defective value on it. This is the sixth leaf found this way, after situsCity, situsZip, landUse, landUseSource and acreage (CTX-LEAVES, CTX-LEAVES2), which is the pattern the card exists to break rather than extend.
completionPredicate: A stranger can evaluate this by running, from this branch, in artifacts/api-server: (1) `npx tsx src/ctxB6VerifySitusAddressCli.ts --self-test` -> failures=0; (2) `DATABASE_URL=<staging read-only> npx tsx src/ctxB6VerifySitusAddressCli.ts` -> exit 0, 12/12, including 48055:1 with isEarnedRecordRetirement=true and refusePayloadAtServe not refusing; (3) the same command with `--violate` -> exit 1; (4) `npx vitest run src/nodeFacetBakeTier1Conformant.test.ts src/lib/__tests__/serveGuardsSitusAddress.test.ts` -> 96 passed. If any of those four disagrees with what is written here, this close is wrong.
scopeBasis: legacy-design-tools only, per the dispatch. hauska-factory was READ (via `git show origin/main:<path>` from its object store, never a worktree) because the grader whose contract this leaf must satisfy lives there and its two S1 regexes had to be reproduced as test fixtures; nothing in it was edited. hauska-engine and hauska-map untouched. The three deliberate exclusions, each with a reason rather than an omission: (a) the StratMap ingest that produces the defective raw string is Factory-side and out of scope, so the fix lands at the PRESENTATION seam in this repo; (b) refusePayloadAtServe is deliberately NOT armed on the new rule until the re-bake, because arming both halves at once would 422 147,199 already-baked rows; (c) retired records keep taking situsForRetiredBake ungated, because CTX-RETIRE ruled the last-known claim must show and CTX-B1 made 48055:1 the regression control for it.

mechanismsConsidered.name: earned absence on the leaf
mechanismsConsidered.why: the only shape that is at once one of the four states, already built and tested here for the strictly more degenerate case, non-destructive under ruling A1 (situsZip and situsCity are separate leaves and untouched; the raw string survives verbatim in the basis), and enforceable AT THE WRITE with a fail-closed assert rather than discovered by a downstream sample.

mechanismsConsidered.name: refuse to assemble an address string when the street component is missing
mechanismsConsidered.whyRejected: THE MEASURED REASON, and it corrects the dispatch: nothing in legacy-design-tools assembles this string. nodeFacetTier1Assemble.ts:334 is `situsAddress: str(input.situsAddress)`; lib/cad-ingest/src/txgio/parse.ts:617 and landuse.ts:173 take `str(properties.SITUS_ADDR)` raw off the StratMap shapefile; pacs/parser.ts:176 uses joinParts(), which DROPS empty components and structurally cannot produce a leading comma; p78Merge.ts COALESCE_FIELDS carries it across unchanged. Proof: 48453:224793's 2026 PACS row carries '4709 SHOALWOOD AVE' while its 2025 StratMap row (source_file stratmap25-landparcels_48453_lp.zip, the county's DECLARED vintage) carries ', TX 78756', and the stored snapshot carries the latter with provenance.parcelVintage 2025. Implemented literally in this repo, 'refuse to assemble' means writing null, which is not a four-state and is exactly what Hays fails on. Implemented at the true assembly site it is a Factory-side StratMap ingest change, out of scope, and would still leave this leaf undefined for a record that genuinely has no street.

mechanismsConsidered.name: keep the string, add a sibling quality/state field
mechanismsConsidered.whyRejected: the leaf the grader and every consumer read would still hold ', TX 78756' as its value; a paying customer still sees a street-less string presented as their address. Also two implementations of one meaning with no divergence test, the CTRL-1 shape.

mechanismsConsidered.name: normalise the string (strip the leading comma, serve 'TX 78756')
mechanismsConsidered.whyRejected: fabricates an address out of a state and a ZIP. The Factory's own S1 rule already classifies the result as a sentinel.

mechanismsConsidered.name: skip the row / refuse the payload
mechanismsConsidered.whyRejected: CTX-SITUS-SKIP (#648) explicitly reversed this. A bad situs is a fact about one leaf, not a reason to discard the row.

theSecondQuestionAnswered.declaredExclusion: this scan measures the STORED payload. The serve mutates zoning and provenance.zoningSource (CTX-MIRROR) and strips envelope, so the stored nulls for those three are not evidence of a served defect. Stated rather than merged into the headline.
theSecondQuestionAnswered.theFindingThatIsWorthMoreThanTheFix: closing the four-state gap does NOT close the defect class, and the measurement says so directly. `", TX 78756"` satisfies BP-CONTENT-01 perfectly: a non-empty string is a `value` under the walk's own classifier. Of the eight named street-less parcels in the live verification run, the Factory's TWO graders together (BP-CONTENT-01 plus the S1 sentinel family) catch FIVE and MISS THREE -- `", TX"` (16,010 Travis rows on that exact string), `", WACO, TX 76705"` (McLennan) and `", CEDAR CREEK, TX 78612"` (Bastrop). Across the whole population the S1 regex pair catches 124,319 of the 147,199 street-less rows, 84.5%, counting rule: rows whose stored situsAddress string matches /^,\s*,/ or /^,\s*TX\s+\d{5}/i, denominator every stored string with an empty pre-first-comma segment. The four-state contract asks whether a cell carries a DECLARED STATE. It does not ask whether the value MEANS anything. Those are two different questions and until this PR only the first had any control at all, and that one on a sample.

lessonsForFleetMemory.text: A four-state contract and a meaning check are different questions. BP-CONTENT-01 grades any non-empty string a `value`, so `", TX 78756"` passes it while being unusable. Closing a four-state gap does not close a content-quality defect class; the write-side content predicate is what does.

A meaning-shaped predicate beat a regex-enumeration by 22,880 rows. hauska-factory's two S1 sentinel regexes catch 84.5% of the street-less population; 'the segment before the first comma holds an alphanumeric' catches 100% by construction, including shapes nobody had written a regex for (`", TX"`, `", WACO, TX 76705"`).

A non-materialized CTE consumed by an N-way UNION ALL is re-inlined N times. A 28-leaf census over a 17 GB table went from 28 full scans (cancelled after 3 minutes with no end in sight) to one 11-minute pass by adding MATERIALIZED. Same class as the recorded PostGIS zone-major lesson.

`provenance.parcelVintage` on a tier-1 payload is the TxGIO PARCEL JOIN vintage, NOT the declared CAD tax year. On Caldwell they differ (2025 vs 2026) and reading the former as the latter makes a retired account read as on-roll. The authoritative record is tryResolveDeclaredCadVintage(fips) in @workspace/cad-ingest.

When widening a fail-closed WRITE control, do not arm the matching SERVE control in the same change. The write control fixes new rows; the serve control would refuse every already-written row until a re-bake, turning an invisible defect into a visible outage.

A stricter 'the street segment must contain a letter' predicate looks better and is worse: it refuses ten real Travis range addresses ('2610, 2612 S 1 ST') to catch six junk rows. Ruling A1 settles it in favour of admitting and naming the residue.
The 170,835 rows are unchanged in the store until the integration seat re-bakes and re-publishes the six counties. Until then a customer still sees ', TX 78756'.

FIXING AN INSTRUMENT DOES NOT FIX THE CONCLUSIONS THAT RESTED ON IT. This lane found mid-work that provenance.parcelVintage is not the declared CAD vintage, filed it as an instrument defect, fixed the instrument, and left standing a close that had drawn its central disposition from the same misreading. Every conclusion that used the field must be re-derived when the field's meaning is corrected. Search the artifact for the wrong reading, do not just patch where it broke.

A tier-1 payload carries THREE vintages and they are easy to confuse: the declared CAD vintage (tryResolveDeclaredCadVintage, what cadRoll dollars/yearBuilt/legal/exemptions report), the parcel-join vintage (provenance.parcelJoin.sourceVintage), and the CLAIM's taxYear (which is what provenance.parcelVintage reports, despite the name). On Travis the claim says 2025 and the declared vintage is 2026.

Before writing an honest-absence over a population, check whether the value exists in a source the same payload ALREADY reads. An absence machinery applied to a recoverable population is worse than the defect it replaces, because absent-verified reads as a positive finding. 139,283 cells were one line of preference away from being deleted by a control built to be honest.

theRealDefect.name: one payload, two vintages
theRealDefect.mechanism: `fetchCountyCadPropertyRoll` filters `WHERE tax_year = <declared>`, and the dollar facets, yearBuilt, legalDescription and exemptionCodes all come from that row. `situsAddress`, `situsCity`, `situsZip` and the acreage claim-fallback come from the cad-parcel-roll ATOM CLAIM instead, which carries whatever vintage the Factory staged. Same bake, two sources, and on Travis the claim is a year stale.
theRealDefect.liveEvidence: 48453:224793, one stored row, read 2026-09-10: marketValue {v:1238899, vintage:'2026', valueBasis:'county-assessed'}, assessedValue vintage '2026', landUse vintage '2026%20preliminary%20appraisal%20export%20supp%200_07072026', situsAddress ', TX 78756', provenance.parcelVintage '2025'. cad_property at declared 2026 carries '4709 SHOALWOOD AVE' (market 1,238,899); the 2025 stratmap25-landparcels row carries ', TX 78756' (market 111,225).
theRealDefect.thePayloadWasAlreadySayingIt: provenance.parcelVintage read '2025' right beside dollars stamped '2026'. The payload self-described the split and nobody read it -- including me, who read it and drew the opposite conclusion.
theRealDefect.consistentWithTheStandingFinding: nothing in this repo composes an address string. That still holds. The defect is in the READ, not in an assembler, which is why the first pass's code archaeology found no composer and still reached the wrong disposition.

theFix.rule: resolveConformantSitusAddress (pure, exported, tested): declared-vintage roll, then claim, then earn an absence.
theFix.whyTheRollWinsEvenOverAUsableClaim: the roll is the vintage this payload's dollars, land use, year built, legal description and exemption codes already report. A payload that mixes vintages across leaves IS the defect; preferring the roll is what makes it single-vintage.
theFix.retiredOrderingIsProven: a roll-absent record takes its branch FIRST, before the roll is consulted at all, so CTX-RETIRE and CTX-B1 are structurally preserved. A test passes a contradictory rollRaw with rollAbsent:true and asserts the retired branch still wins -- the ordering is proven, not trusted.
theFix.noSecondQuery: TRUE, and checked rather than assumed. `cadPropertyRoll.byPropId` is loaded once before the per-row loop and is the same map the dollar path uses. The ROW was already in hand; the COLUMN was not selected. One column (`situs_address`) was added to that existing SELECT in fetchCountyCadPropertyRoll. No new query, no second pass over cad_property.
theFix.provenanceSoItCannotRegressInvisibly: provenance.situsAddressSource (declared-roll | claim | retired-claim | none) and provenance.situsAddressSupersededClaim (the claim value the roll overrode, when they differ). Plus per-run counters situsFromDeclaredRoll / situsFromClaim / situsRollSupersededClaim and a log line naming every source. Without these, a re-bake that quietly stopped preferring the roll would look identical to one that preferred it.
theFix.allowlistPinFired: DIVERGENCE_ALLOWLIST_NEW_SHAPE_PREFIXES has a pin test asserting the exact list. Adding the two provenance keys FAILED it, which is the control working: widening that allowlist is a deliberate act with a written reason, never a silent one.

measuredRecoverability.countingRule: every stored node-facets:tier1 row in the six counties whose baseFacts.situsAddress is a bare null or a string with no alphanumeric before its first comma, LEFT JOINed to cad_property at THAT COUNTY's declared tax_year (48021 2025, 48055 2026, 48209 2026, 48309 2025, 48453 2026, 48491 2026). 'recoverable' = the declared-roll row carries a situs_address that passes the same street predicate.
measuredRecoverability.independentAgreement: 139,256 reproduces the coordinator's figure exactly, from an instrument written before seeing theirs. The 27 Hays bare-nulls are ADDITIONAL: the reopening framed the population as street-less strings only, and the same read-source defect reaches the bare-null population too.
measuredRecoverability.whyOnlyTravis: Bastrop and McLennan are declared 2025, so their claims and their rolls are the same vintage and agree. Caldwell's and Hays's street-less rows are 100% retired (no declared-roll row to recover from). Travis is the only county in this set whose declared vintage moved to a cad-export while its staged claim stayed on the prior StratMap drop.

theSiblingQuestionAnswered.notFixedHere_andWhy: situsCity feeds `resolveZoningJurisdiction` as the jurisdiction fallback, so changing it moves zoning-jurisdiction assignment for ~78k parcels and would silently re-key zoning provenance. That is not something to slip into this card. acreage's absences are mostly `refused`/`lookup-failed`, which DECLARE that nothing was measured -- honest about their stated scope, and so a materially smaller lie than situsAddress's `absent-verified`. Each needs its own card with its own regression control.
theSiblingQuestionAnswered.theHonestCharacterisation: the situsCity/situsZip absences are scoped to `claim.situsCity` in their own basis text, so they are literally true about the claim and wrong about the parcel. That is what makes them survive BP-CONTENT-01: a four-state check reads the declared state, not whether the scope the absence chose was the right scope to search.

theValuationQuestionAnswered.question: Does the claim-versus-roll split explain any part of the Travis valuation gap?
theValuationQuestionAnswered.instruction: asked to say whether my read of the code makes it plausible or rules it out, without investigating.
theValuationQuestionAnswered.answer: RULED OUT for the baked tier-1 payload; NOT ruled out for any consumer that reads the atom body directly.
theValuationQuestionAnswered.codeBasis: `readConformantCadClaim` does parse the claim's marketValue/assessedValue/landValue/improvementValue/livingAreaSqft into ConformantCadClaim (lines 258-262), but the builder never consumes them: `baseFacts.cadRoll` comes from `cadPropertyFactsFromRow(cadPropRow)`, and cadPropRow is the declared-vintage roll row. Grep for `claim.marketValue` and its four siblings returns only the reader. So the baked dollars are declared-vintage and stamped with it.
theValuationQuestionAnswered.whatIsNotRuledOut: the CLAIM demonstrably carries the stale StratMap dollars -- 48453:224793's 2025 row is market 111,225 against the 2026 row's 1,238,899, an 11x gap on one parcel. Any surface reading the hauska_mcp atom body rather than the baked tier-1 payload would see the 111,225. That is outside this repo and outside this card; named, not investigated.
theValuationQuestionAnswered.caveat: this is a code-read, not a measurement. Per ENFORCEMENT, a code-read outranks output-measuring when they disagree, but it is still a claim about reachability that a structural instrument should confirm before anyone acts on it.
